narrative.overview:
The design language of go-phish is the intelligence brief: a document that conveys authority through density and structure, not through visual polish. Every surface is a flat page. Presence comes from the weight of the information on it, not from the interface's self-decoration.

The system is almost entirely achromatic. Geist Variable carries the hierarchy through weight and scale contrast. Color appears only when it means something: threat signals are vermilion, safe signals are green, outbound tool calls are blue, caution states are amber. The four signals form a directional vocabulary — if you see color, the system is telling you something.

This rejects three named failure modes: the SaaS dashboard aesthetic, the security-tool cliché (green-on-black terminal cosplay, red-alert banners on every state), and the clinical blank. The Intelligence Brief has presence because a serious document has presence.
keyCharacteristics: Achromatic by default; color is always signal, never decoration
Hierarchy through type weight and scale, not cards or chrome
Flat surfaces — borders and tonal contrast convey depth, no shadows

rules.name: The Four Signals Rule
rules.body: The only chromatic colors are Alert Vermilion, Clear Green, Dispatch Blue, and Standby Amber. These are reserved for threat/failure, nominal/complete, outbound direction, and caution states respectively. A new state that doesn't fit one of these four is expressed through typography, not a fifth color.

rules.name: The No Tint Rule
rules.body: Neutral surfaces are pure achromatic OKLCH (chroma = 0). No hue-tinted backgrounds, branded fills, or gradient overlays on containers. The page is a document. Documents don't glow.

rules.name: The Mono Discipline Rule
rules.body: Monospace is reserved for machine-produced data: investigation IDs, raw URLs, tool call inputs/outputs, artifact content. Never on prose labels, navigation, or headings.

rules.name: The One Headline Rule
rules.body: Every view has exactly one Headline (600/1.5rem). If content needs emphasis, use Body Strong or Title — never a custom intermediate size.

rules.name: The Flat Document Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow on any resting surface. Use border-border or bg-muted fills for distinction. The system is a document, not a 3D stage.

dos: Do reserve the four signal colors for their exact assigned roles.
Do show evidence text by default on every claim block — never hidden behind a toggle at rest.
Do use monospace exclusively for machine-produced data.
Do keep all surfaces flat; use tonal contrast and borders for depth.
Do conform to WCAG AA: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for UI components.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion for live stream animations.
donts: Don't use SaaS dashboard patterns: gradient cards, hero metrics, identical icon-heading-text grids.
Don't use security-tool clichés: green-on-black terminal, red-alert banners on non-failure states.
Don't produce a clinical blank form — presence comes from typography and spacing.
Don't add a sixth signal color.
Don't add box-shadow to resting surfaces.
Don't use gradient text, glassmorphism, or side-stripe borders (border-left > 1px as accent).
Don't add dark mode — explicitly out of scope for v1.
Don't use border-left > 1px as a colored accent stripe on any component.
